visuals: A sunny Curaçao beach with white sand, palm trees, and calm, crystal-clear turquoise water under a bright blue sky. No text, no signs, no written words.
script:
Curaçao gets more sunshine than most Caribbean islands.
With warm breezes and clear water, every day feels like a beach day!

visuals: Waves crashing into giant sea caves and soaring rocky cliffs at Shete Boka National Park in Curaçao. No text, no signs, no written words.
script:
Now for my favorite part… nature! Shete Boka National Park is wild and wonderful. Imagine waves crashing into giant sea caves and soaring cliffs. 
Epic, right?

visuals: A bright pink Caribbean flamingo standing gracefully in the shallow turquoise waters of a Curaçao lagoon. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Soar like a flamingo!! Because the Caribbean flamingo is the island’s colorful feathered icon.

visuals: A green iguana sunbathing on a warm rock in the tropical landscape of Curaçao. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: You might also spot a green iguana, called “yuana” by locals, lounging in the sun or popping up in traditions.

visuals: The colorful Handelskade waterfront in CuraçAo bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Speaking of animals, get this: dolphins swim off the coast.

visuals: A tiny, colorful hummingbird zipping through tropical flowers in a Curaçao garden. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And hummingbirds zip through gardens. A bird and a fish doing a beauty contest? Now that’s a show!

visuals: The iconic Handelskade waterfront in Willemstad, Curaçao, with its rainbow-colored Dutch colonial buildings along the harbor. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Ready for the capital? Drumroll please… it’s Willemstad! Ever seen buildings that look like a rainbow? This port city is full of Dutch-style houses in every pastel color. It’s like Legoland met the Caribbean!

visuals: The coastal village of Sint Michiel in Curaçao with its quiet beach and small fishing boats. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Visit Sint Michiel for amazing snorkeling.

visuals: A vibrant local food festival in Tera Kòrá, Curaçao, with stalls and people enjoying the music. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Or check out local food festivals in Tera Kòrá. It’s yum and fun rolled into one!

visuals: Playa Knip beach in CuraçAo bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Curaçao is a language party! Folks speak Papiamentu, Dutch, English, and Spanish. Four languages on one island? Multilingual magic!

visuals: Queen Emma Bridge in CuraçAo bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: About 160,000 people live here. That’s enough people to fill two giant football stadiums!

visuals: A traditional Curaçao keshi yena (stuffed cheese) served in a rustic clay bowl on a wooden table. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Time to eat! Hungry? Try keshi yena! A cheesy dish stuffed with spiced meat. It’s often shared at family celebrations and tastes like a hug in a bowl.

visuals: A sunny beachside stall in Curaçao selling fruity batidos in bright cups under a thatched roof. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Need to cool off? Grab a batido! These fruity smoothies come in flavors like mango, papaya, or coconut, sold at sunny beach stalls. Slurp!

visuals: A local street vendor's cart in Curaçao displaying golden-fried pastechi pastries to customers. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Still hungry? Street stalls also serve pastechi! Golden pastries stuffed with cheese or meat. One bite and you'll be doing the happy dance!

visuals: A grand Carnival parade in Curaçao with dancers in elaborate feathered costumes and confetti under a tropical sun. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Wanna dance for real? Check out Carnival! It’s Curaçao’s biggest celebration, with dazzling parades, live music, and colorful costumes. It can last several days… or even a few weeks!

visuals: Curaçao musicians playing traditional instruments like drums and maracas on an outdoor stage at dusk. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Feel the beat of the traditional music! African drums and European sounds create a worldwide playlist you can dance to.

visuals: An aerial view of the historic Willemstad harbor in Curaçao with ships passing the colorful waterfront buildings. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And guess what? Willemstad’s harbor is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It’s more than pretty. It’s packed with history and pride.

visuals: Curaçao baseball star Kenley Jansen in professional gear on a pitcher's mound. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Sports fans, listen up! Kenley Jansen, a Major League Baseball star originally from Curaçao, is known for his time with the LA Dodgers.

visuals: Curaçao soccer player Cuco Martina in his national team uniform on the pitch. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And Cuco Martina, a Curaçao soccer star, has played across Europe!

visuals: The floating Queen Emma Bridge in Willemstad, Curaçao, swung open across the water with pedestrians waiting on the side. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Here’s a cool curveball: the Queen Emma Bridge floats and swings open for boats! Locals call it “The Swinging Old Lady!” How’s that for wild design?
